title: Publish to moe/release/<goalId> when the workspace branch is the remote's default branch, or when that default is unknown
description:
ROW 2 of 3 for task-4ba1e00a3aa64a83a1b883566377e3ab, filed by architect-73d103f8 on 2026-09-18 under the owner's choice of OPTION A. Depends on task-baefab32f1264daf8f173efc0c1fe2c0, which measures and records a remote's default branch and exports `readRemoteDefaultBranch(store, projectId, remoteUrl): string | null`. task-4ba1e00a (the release guard, the card, the live test and docs) depends on this row.

THE DEFECT THIS ROW CLOSES (measured live on UnAI 2026-09-18). The lander commits every accepted node onto the workspace branch; the publish candidate is that workspace's `symbolic-ref HEAD` (apps/daemon/src/repository/publication-candidate.ts:21); and the push is `${sha}:refs/heads/${candidate.approval.branch}` (git-publication-port.ts:66). On UnAI the workspace branch IS the remote's default (`master`), so publish pushes straight onto the operator's default branch, and Release can then never open a PR - head equals base, and the code is already there.

THE ONE SEAM. The whole publish pipeline is keyed on `candidate.approval.branch`: `push` targets it, `observe` ls-remotes it (:77), node-publisher.ts:68-73 records the PUSHED receipt with it and CHECKS the receipt matches, release-decide-service.ts `pushedBranchOf` (:85-108) reads that receipt's branch as its PR head, and apps/daemon/src/http/repository-remote-read.ts:105 shows `approval` to the operator, who approves exactly that object. So set the target ONCE, in the candidate: when the recorded remote default is UNKNOWN (null) or EQUALS the workspace branch, `approval.branch` becomes `moe/release/<goalId>`; otherwise it stays the workspace branch, exactly as today. Push, observe, receipt, release head and the operator's approval screen then all follow with no change of their own - and the operator APPROVES THE REAL TARGET, rather than approving `master` while Moe pushes something else.

WHY UNKNOWN MAPS TO THE RELEASE BRANCH (epic rail 4). Pushing onto an existing branch that might be the operator's default is the risky act; an unmeasured default is not evidence that it is safe, so it gains no authority to do it. The cost is deliberate and bounded: a project whose default has not yet been measured publishes its first goal to `moe/release/<goalId>` even if its workspace is on a feature branch.

THE READER SIGNATURE CHANGES, and that is a shape change with named consumers. `PublicationCandidateReader` is `(remoteUrl) => ...` today (declared in publication-approval-contracts.ts) and knows no goalId. It must also receive the goalId and the recorded default, so preview, command and push all compute the SAME target from the SAME recorded inputs - the operator's approval must equal a fresh candidate read at preview (repository-remote-read.ts:100), at command (`samePublicationApproval`, publish-services.ts:95-100) and at push (node-publisher.ts:33, :53). Known implementers and callers: publication-candidate.ts, publish-services.ts, repository-remote-read.ts, node-publisher.ts, and the fixture at apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:214. Census the whole tree before planning; if the callers exceed the path cap, split.

`moe/release/<goalId>` must be a valid ref for every goalId the store can hold - validate with `git check-ref-format --branch` semantics and refuse by name rather than push a ref git would reject.

OUT OF SCOPE: measuring the default (task-baefab32), the RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE guard, the Release card and docs (task-4ba1e00a). Deleting accumulated `moe/release/*` branches from remotes after merge is a follow-up.
definitionOfDone: With the recorded default EQUAL to the workspace branch, the candidate's `approval.branch` is exactly `moe/release/<goalId>`; with the default UNKNOWN (null) it is also `moe/release/<goalId>`; with a DIFFERENT known default it is the workspace branch unchanged - one arm per case, asserting the branch by value against the production candidate reader.

Preview, command and push agree: an arm drives the same goal through repository-remote-read, the publish command and node-publisher with the same recorded default and asserts all three produce an identical approval, and that the command accepts the preview's approval (no PUBLISH_CANDIDATE_CHANGED). A second arm changes the recorded default between preview and command and asserts the exact refusal PUBLISH_CANDIDATE_CHANGED with its layer.
A goalId that cannot form a valid ref is refused by name before any push, never pushed.
Every implementer and caller of PublicationCandidateReader is updated and named in the completion record with a whole-tree census; no fixture is left implementing the old signature.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed` count lines: daemon tests for src/repository/**, src/http/repository-remote-read*, src/orchestrator/node-publisher*, and `pnpm typecheck`.

implementationPlan.description: Refuse an invalid ref by name (DoD 3). Invalid names return a NAMED refusal through `publicationRefused` and never a candidate, so nothing downstream can push a ref git would reject or quietly rewrite.    - A measurement that lands between preview and command gives STALE (arm 2), and the operator re-previews.
3. Goals decided BEFORE this row: node-publisher decodes the stored decision (publish-ledger.ts decodeRequest) and never re-reads. Recovery therefore pushes the recorded workspace branch unchanged. The intent check at node-publisher.ts:194 compares recorded values only.
4. Case sensitivity: releaseBranch uses `!==` and readRemoteDefaultBranch returns the stored string. No toLowerCase, toUpperCase or localeCompare appears in the 7 files of the chain. The `Master` vs `master` arm answers `Master`.
5. Can an invalid ref reach `git push`? No.
   - The reader refuses PUBLISH_RELEASE_BRANCH_INVALID. Its validPublicationBranch rule is swept against real `git check-ref-format --branch` over 19 names.
   - The command records only decodePublicationCandidate output, which re-validates the branch.
   - node-publisher decodes again before it pushes.
   - A reader refusal at the command surfaces as `<code>` @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE (publish-services.ts:97).
6. Ceiling, out of scope and owned by task-4ba1e00a (RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE): a default re-measured AFTER the command commits does not change an approved push. That is by design: the push is the approval.

CORRECTIONS to the description and DoD
(a) The push does not re-read the candidate, so only TWO production readers pass the target, not three. node-publisher.ts:33 and :53 compare recorded values.
(b) DoD 2's code: the command refuses `PUBLISH_APPROVAL_STALE` @ `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` (publish-services.ts:99-101). `PUBLISH_CANDIDATE_CHANGED` is emitted only by the reader, when the repository moves mid-read. The arms assert the production code.
(c) DoD 2 says "through node-publisher". The arms assert this at node-publisher's own read seam (readPublishLedger), together with the existing pin at node-publisher.test.ts:123.

LINE REFS: both production files keep their line counts, because each type import was merged inline into its value import. So publish-services.ts:72, :86, :89, :99-101 and :103, cited in tests/e2e and bootstrap-durability.test.ts, still point at the right lines.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Filed by me earlier today as leaf 2 of the owner-chosen OPTION A for task-4ba1e00a. dependsOn task-baefab32 (which lands `readRemoteDefaultBranch`), which itself waits on task-78dea88b. Measured at HEAD 2026-09-18; step 1's re-measure is binding because both prerequisites rewrite files this row reads.

(1) A CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN DESCRIPTION, measured. The description says the approval must equal a fresh candidate read 'at push (node-publisher.ts:33, :53)'. It does NOT. node-publisher's `PublishRequest` is DECODED FROM THE STORED DECISION (apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-ledger.ts:66 `decodeRequest(decision)`), and the publish command records the candidate — `approval.branch` included — in that decision (publish-services.ts:106 and the event payload at :110). node-publisher.ts:33 and :53 compare the REQUEST's recorded candidate with the INTENT's recorded candidate; neither calls the reader. So the push inherits whatever branch the COMMAND recorded, and there are TWO production readers, not three: the preview (apps/daemon/src/http/repository-remote-read.ts:100) and the command (apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-services.ts:95). The command then requires the operator's approval — taken from the preview — to equal its own fresh read via `samePublicationApproval` (:100).

(2) THE READER AND ITS FULL CENSUS. `export type PublicationCandidateReader = (remoteUrl: string) => PublicationCandidateResult;` (publication-approval-contracts.ts:19). `git grep -n "PublicationCandidateReader\|readPublicationCandidate\|createPublicationCandidateReader" -- apps tests` returns eleven daemon references — more than the description listed: the declaration; the implementer publication-candidate.ts; the two production callers above; pass-through type references in daemon-command-registry.ts:18/:130/:283, daemon-repository-workflow-wiring.ts:32 and daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:288/:575; and test callers — bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:214 (implements it and SPREADS `remoteUrl` as a string), repository-publication-read.test.ts:13 and publication-approval.test.ts:25/:104 (zero-argument fakes), and git-publication-native.test.ts:45/:56 (CALLS it with a bare string). The control-room's `readPublicationCandidate` (apps/control-room/src/live/live-publication-candidate.ts:17) is an UNRELATED function of the same name that fetches over HTTP; it is not this type.

(3) WHY AN OPTIONAL SECOND PARAMETER. Changing the reader to take an object would break git-publication-native.test.ts (a string argument) and bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts (which uses its argument as a string). An OPTIONAL trailing `target` leaves every one of those valid and unchanged, and gives callers that do not pass it exactly today's behaviour. The risk is a production caller that FORGETS it and silently keeps pushing to the default branch; the preview-command agreement arm in step 4 exists to catch exactly that, because a forgotten target makes the two disagree.

(4) WHERE THE DEFAULT COMES FROM. Both production callers hold `store` and `projectId` (repository-remote-read's port is built with them at daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:575; the command's handler reads the store, as publish-services.ts's `bindingLeg` does) and call task-baefab32's `readRemoteDefaultBranch(store, projectId, remoteUrl)` — a LOCAL store read, safe on the polled preview path.

(5) THE READER RUNS GIT SYNCHRONOUSLY. publication-candidate.ts (34 lines) already runs `execFileSync("git", ...)` for `rev-parse` and `symbolic-ref`, so ref validation may reuse that runner; no async path is needed.
